identity.name: Sodium o-phenylphenol (Sodium orthophenylphenol)
identity.chemical_class: Aromatic phenolic preservative (sodium salt of o-phenylphenol)

function.mechanism: Phenolic antimicrobial/fungicidal action; used to reduce post-harvest fungal spoilage on treated fruit surfaces.
common_food_categories: food-contact paper and paperboard manufacturing (defoaming-agent formulations)

adi.basis: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation for orthophenylphenol/sodium orthophenylphenol; ADI derived from toxicology dataset with nephrotoxicity/body-weight effects as key drivers.

efsa.key_finding: Use at reported levels as post-harvest fungicides for citrus fruits was not a safety concern when peel is not consumed; conservative combined exposure scenarios could exceed ADI.

fda.notes: Listed in defoaming-agent formulations for paper/paperboard used with food, with use limited to technical effect; no direct GRAS listing for this term was identified in searched Title 21 text.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database entry reports ADI 0-0.2 mg/kg bw for sodium o-phenylphenol (evaluation year shown: 1964).

concerns.summary: IARC classification dataset lists sodium ortho-phenylphenate as Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans).
Recent zebrafish studies report developmental cardiotoxicity and craniofacial toxicity linked to impaired progenitor cell migration and oxidative stress pathways under OPP exposure.

In reconstructed human skin/airway biocide models including 2-phenylphenol, airway viability reductions were observed for several biocides, indicating inhalation/irritation concern in non-dietary exposure contexts.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation concluded no concern for genotoxicity.
EFSA reported no adverse effects in a two-generation reproductive study at tested doses.

populations: high consumers of citrus peel-containing products
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported conservative combined exposure estimates above ADI in some scenarios; safety concern was not identified when treated peel is not consumed.

risk_assessment.rationale: E232 has established ADIs and conditional regulatory acceptance, but not an unrestricted safety profile. Conservative exposure scenarios can exceed ADI, IARC classifies sodium ortho-phenylphenate as Group 2B, and recent mechanistic toxicology studies report developmental toxicity signals in model organisms.
key_factors: EFSA ADI 0.15 mg/kg bw/day with conditional safety conclusion tied to peel consumption assumptions
Evidence of developmental/mechanistic toxicity in recent zebrafish studies
Specific-use FDA CFR authorization rather than broad direct GRAS context
